 WVLA Baton Rouge Follow DOJ: East Baton Rouge chosen to receive federal money to boost public safety
 Allison Bruhl Fri, October 30, 2026 at 7:32 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. DOJ: East Baton Rouge chosen to receive federal money to boost public safety BATON ROUGE, La. ( Louisiana First ) -- East Baton Rouge Parish was one of four places chosen to receive a portion of $300 million from a federal initiative targeting violent crime.
 The Model Cities Initiative (MCI), announced in June, aims to strengthen public safety by helping local law enforcement, local government officials, and community partners form comprehensive strategies. According to the Department of Justice (DOJ), applications from selected cities showed innovation.
  90+ arrests after summer Baton Rouge area operation targeting violent crime and drug trafficking  
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Other cities chosen: Jacksonville, Florida; Jackson, Mississippi; and St. Louis, Missouri.
 "These cities are setting an example of proactive law enforcement that will strengthen the rule of law and improve public safety in their jurisdictions. As violent crime rates continue to fall to historic lows, the Department of Justice is redoubling our efforts to invest in local communities and keep American families safe," U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said.
 The East Baton Rouge Parish Coroner's Office reports 86 homicides in the parish as of Oct. 26. Baton Rouge Police Chief TJ Morse told Louisiana First News in December 2025 the city had seen a decline in overall crime rates, crediting part of the reduction to keeping repeat offenders off the streets.
 The Baton Rouge Police Department could add 50-60 new officers in the new year after an uptick in applicants sparked by historic pay raises approved in the spring . The department became the highest-paid in Louisiana, now offering $58,000 base pay for new officers. Before the raises, Morse warned of a shortage of at least 150 officers.
 Advertisement Advertisement The DOJ will work with each city to implement public safety plans. Money could go toward:
 Hiring sworn and non-sworn law enforcement officers and other personnel
 Adopting new and improved technology
 Purchasing or leasing equipment
 Enhancing forensic capabilities and capacity
 Providing services to address mental health and substance use issues
  Leaders converge at Louisiana Public Safety Summit to discuss crime, policy  
 Blanche plans to travel to Louisiana in November to meet with Baton Rouge leaders.
 Read statements from Louisiana leaders
 Sen. Bill Cassidy celebrated East Baton Rouge's success in securing funding.
 "Anytime a city receives tens of millions to make it a safer, better place to be, that is fantastic news. I look forward to this money helping Baton Rouge, but also as a model to other communities as well. Compliments to the mayor, the district attorney, and others for entering a winning application. I am proud to have supported their effort."
 Congresswoman Julia Letlow said she was proud to work with leaders in the push for safer streets.
 "Congratulations to the City of Baton Rouge and Mayor Sid Edwards for successfully securing a sizable share of this $300 million nationwide initiative. I was proud to work with the City and the Trump Administration to help put more officers on our streets, give law enforcement the tools they need to fight violent crime, and make Baton Rouge a safer place for families to live, work, and raise their children," 
 Cassidy and Letlow wrote a joint Sept. 1 letter of support to the MCI selection panel.
